title: Tensors
outline: Lecture 14 video (Data Science, COM3021): 'Tensors'. 11 scenes, 128 s, built from videos/_plan/ds-14-script.md. STORY in the lessons' order: 14.1 ds14-orders (scene 2), 14.2 ds14-shapes (scene 3), 14.3 ds14-sparse (scenes 4 and 5), 14.4 ds14-keys (scene 6), 14.5 ds14-csr (scenes 7 and 8), 14.6 ds14-csc (scene 9), when to use each (scene 10), recap and 'Next: Workshop 14.W'. Running example: Sprout, the seed-swap app. CHANGE from the script: scene 6 builds the dictionary of keys and the coordinate list from the 4 x 4 matrix it shows (the slides' M9: keys (0,0) 5, (1,1) 8, (2,2) 3, (3,1) 6; lookup (3,1) gives 6, missing (3,2) gives 0) instead of the slides' unrelated (0,0) -> 1.0 ... (1,5) -> 11.0 example, so the picture and the list agree. NUMBERS: every figure comes from videos/d14/common.js (VID.d14), which ports the lessons' formats() and sheet() and asserts the values at load. COLOURS: grey zeros, grid lines, arrows, plain labels; blue stored values (V / VALUES); orange positions (index numbers, keys, COL_INDEX in CSR, ROW_INDEX in CSC, shape names); purple bookmarks and directions (ROW_INDEX in CSR, COL_PTR in CSC, index arrows, order counter); green the answer (a row or column read back, the smaller store, ticks); red waste (the bigger store, the n x n square).

titleCard.title: Tensors
titleCard.sub: One number, a row, a grid, a pile of grids

title: Count the indices
you need to find one value
caps: Sprout's thermometer: 18°. One number is a scalar.
One member's ratings, 3, 5, 1, 4: a vector.
Rows under rows: a matrix. Two indices find a value.
A pile of grids is a 3-order tensor: three indices.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 2 (THE ORDER OF A TENSOR): one figure grows in place, and the order counts the indices needed to find one value (lesson 14.1). Data from D14.ORD. Colours: blue the values, purple the index arrows and the order counter, grey the plain label, green-tinted and purple-tinted outlines for the grids stacked behind. Story (local seconds): 0.5 one blue cube "18°" (the greenhouse thermometer), "order 0", "scalar · 0 indices"; 3.0 the cube flips to 3 and 5, 1, 4 pop in beside it, a purple arrow along the row, "order 1"; 5.8 two more rows drop in below, the row arrow slides under the grid, a second purple arrow down the side, "order 2"; 8.8 two copies of the grid slide in behind (purple and green outlines), a third purple arrow into the depth, "order 3". Hold to 14.

title: Name the directions,
and you know the shape
caps: A packet's features: one vector.
Sensor readings: features × timestamps, a matrix.
A photo: width × height × channels (RGB).
A video: frames × width × height × channels.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 3 (THE SHAPES OF DATA): four panels build one after the other, each with its shape in orange underneath (lesson 14.2). Data from D14.SHAPE. Colours: blue the values, orange the shape names, purple the "order 4" badge, red / green / blue the colour channels of a photo, grey the panel frames and plain labels. Story (local seconds): 0.5 panel 1, the sweet pea packet's card: four features with blue values 180, 10, 150, 7, "features"; 3.4 panel 2, the soil sensor: rows moisture and soil °C, one column of readings slides in per beat (6am to 9pm), "features × timestamps"; 6.6 panel 3, a photo as three stacked channel grids R, G, B, "width × height × channels"; 9.6 panel 4, four frames (each a small R G B stack), "frames × width × height × channels", then the purple badge "order 4". Hold to 14.

title: Mostly zeros,
or mostly filled
caps: Sprout's swap sheet: 6 non-zeros of 64. Sparsity 91%.
Listing only the non-zeros: 18 numbers instead of 64.
Fill it to 52: dense, sparsity 19%.
Now the list, 156 numbers, is bigger than the grid.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 4 (SPARSE OR DENSE): Sprout's 8 x 8 swap sheet fills up; sparsity and the cost of a list of non-zeros against the full grid (lesson 14.3, its sparsityLab demo). Cells fill in the lesson's fixed order (D14.SHEET.fill). Colours: grey the zeros and plain labels, blue the non-zero cells and their counter, orange the sparsity, green the smaller store, red the bigger one. Story (local seconds): 0.2 the grey sheet; 0.5-3.3 six cells fill one by one, the counters follow (6 non-zeros, sparsity 91%), "sparse: mostly 0"; 4.2 two bars: red "Full grid: 64 numbers", green "Non-zero list: 18 numbers"; 7.6-10.0 the sheet fills to 52 cells, the counters run to 52 and 19%, the label turns to "dense: mostly filled", the list bar grows past the grid bar to 156 and turns red while the grid bar turns green. Hold to 13.

title: Real data is full of gaps,
and too big to write out
caps: A social graph: 5 links out of 15 possible.
Fault sensors report 0 almost all the time.
n ≈ a million: a million million cells. Too big to store.
Keep only the non-zeros instead.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 5 (WHY IT MATTERS): real data is sparse, and storing every zero of a big matrix is impossible (lesson 14.3). Data from D14.BIG. Colours: grey the members, links, sensor and plain labels, blue the one non-zero reading, red the full n × n store, green the non-zeros-only store. Story (local seconds): 0.5 six grey member circles A to F, 0.9-2.9 five links draw one by one, "5 links of 15 possible"; 3.4 a fault sensor and its strip of ten readings, one blue 1 among the 0s, "almost always 0"; 5.8 both slide up and away, a red square "every cell: n × n numbers" grows, with "n ≈ 1,000,000" and "a million million cells, 64-bit each"; 8.0 a grey arrow to a small green box "non-zeros only: about n entries". Hold to 11.

scenes.kicker: DICTIONARY OF KEYS AND COORDINATE LIST
title: Keep the values,
remember where they live
caps: Store only the non-zeros, each with its position.
Dictionary of keys: each (row, column) key maps to its value.
Look up key (3, 1): 6. A missing key means 0.
Coordinate list: a list of (row, column, value) tuples.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 6 (DICTIONARY OF KEYS AND COORDINATE LIST): keep the non-zeros with their positions (lesson 14.4). The list is built from the slides' 4 x 4 matrix shown beside it (D14.M9, D14.F9.nz), so the picture and the list agree (the slides' separate (0,0) -> 1.0 example is not used). Colours: grey zeros, arrows and the header, blue the values, orange the positions (index numbers, keys, row and column of a tuple), green the value found, grey "0" for a missing key. Story (local seconds): 0.5 the matrix with orange row and column numbers, the four non-zeros pulse; 3.2 it slides left and the "dictionary of keys" list builds, one row every 0.5 s: orange key, grey arrow, blue value; 6.0 a magnifier hops onto key (3, 1), its value 6 turns green and the matrix cell gets a green ring; 7.4 a missing key (3, 2) is tried and returns a grey 0; 8.8 the header becomes "coordinate list" and each row becomes a (row, column, value) tuple of three chips. Hold to 13.

title: Values, columns,
and bookmarks for each row
caps: Read row by row: V = 5, 8, 3, 6; COL_INDEX = 0, 1, 2, 1.
ROW_INDEX marks where each row starts in V: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.
m rows need m + 1 bookmarks: the last marks the end.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 7 (COMPRESSED SPARSE ROW): read the slides' 4 x 4 matrix row by row into V, COL_INDEX and ROW_INDEX (lesson 14.5). Data from D14.M9 / D14.F9 (the lesson's formats()). Colours: grey zeros and the reading cursor, blue the values (V), orange the columns (COL_INDEX and the column numbers), purple the bookmarks (ROW_INDEX, the ticks above V, the brace). Story (local seconds): 0.2 matrix and empty arrays; 0.5-4.5 a cursor reads the 16 cells row by row (0.25 s a cell); at each non-zero a blue packet flies into V and an orange packet (its column number) into COL_INDEX; 4.9-6.9 ROW_INDEX fills 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (one every 0.5 s) while a purple tick drops above V where that row starts and the matrix row gets a purple ring; 8.4 a purple brace under ROW_INDEX "4 rows: 5 entries (m + 1)"; 9.4 the last entry pulses, "the last marks the end". Hold to 13.

title: Open at one bookmark,
stop at the next
caps: Read row 2 of the slides' 4 × 6 matrix.
Start = ROW_INDEX[2] = 4, end = ROW_INDEX[3] = 7.
Slice V: 50, 60, 70 at columns 2, 3, 4.
Equal bookmarks, 2 and 2: an empty slice, an all-zero row.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 8 (READING A ROW BACK): rebuild row 2 of the slides' 4 x 6 matrix from its CSR arrays, then an empty row (lesson 14.5, "Read a row back"). Data from D14.M12 / F12 / R2 and D14.M3 / F3 / R3. Colours: grey zeros, blue the values (V), orange the columns (COL_INDEX), purple the bookmarks (ROW_INDEX), green the slice and the rebuilt row. Story (local seconds): 0.5 the matrix (row 2 still empty, dashed) and its three arrays; 2.4 ROW_INDEX[2] = 4 and ROW_INDEX[3] = 7 glow purple, "start 4", "end 7"; 4.8 a green frame covers positions 4 to 6 of V and COL_INDEX; 7.0 the values 50, 60, 70 fly into row 2 at columns 2, 3, 4, the other cells of the row turn grey 0, a green tick; 9.4-10.0 the picture changes to the 3 x 3 matrix with an empty middle row: ROW_INDEX 0, 2, 2, 3; 10.4 the two middle bookmarks (2 and 2) glow purple, 10.9 a grey dashed frame on the all-zero middle row and "empty slice: all 0". Hold to 14.

title: The same trick,
turned on its side
caps: CSC reads column by column: VALUES = 10, 2, 5, 7, 9.
COL_PTR marks where each column starts: 0, 2, 3, 4, 5.
Column 0: from 0 to 2, so 10 at row 0 and 2 at row 3.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 9 (COMPRESSED SPARSE COLUMN): read the slides' 4 x 4 matrix column by column into VALUES, ROW_INDEX and COL_PTR, then read column 0 back (lesson 14.6). Data from D14.M13 / F13 / C0 (the lesson's formats()). Colours: grey zeros and the reading cursor, blue the values (VALUES), orange the rows (ROW_INDEX and the row numbers), purple the bookmarks (COL_PTR, the ticks above VALUES), green the column read back. Story (local seconds): 0.2 matrix and empty arrays; 0.5-4.5 a cursor reads the 16 cells column by column, top to bottom (0.25 s a cell); at each non-zero a blue packet flies into VALUES and an orange packet (its row number) into ROW_INDEX; 4.6-6.2 COL_PTR fills 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 (one every 0.4 s), a purple tick drops above VALUES where that column starts and the matrix column gets a purple ring; 7.0 COL_PTR[0] and COL_PTR[1] glow; 7.5 a green frame covers VALUES and ROW_INDEX 0 to 1; 8.1-8.9 the two values fly into column 0 at rows 0 and 3 (green rings); 9.1 a green frame on column 0 and a tick. Hold to 11.

title: Store it
the way you will read it
caps: CSR: fast row operations. A graph row is one node's neighbours.
Good for row slicing and many A × x products.
CSC: fast column operations, like 'who swapped tomato?'
Good for huge datasets with many categorical features.
scenes.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 10 (CSR OR CSC): store the matrix the way you will read it (lessons 14.5 and 14.6, when to use each). Data from D14.CHOOSE. Colours: blue the CSR card and the stored 1s, orange the CSC card, grey zeros, links, names and the use tags, purple the row-by-row sweep of A × x, green the row or column that answers a question, red "slow for one column". Story (local seconds): 0.5 the blue card "CSR: fast rows": a small adjacency grid (rows and columns A, B, C, D for Ada, Ben, Cy, Dot) and the graph beside it, Ada linked to Ben, Cy and Dot; 1.6 Ada's row glows green, "Ada's row: Ben, Cy, Dot"; 3.6 grey tags "row slicing" and "many A × x products" while a purple frame sweeps the grid row by row; 6.2 the orange card "CSC: fast columns": a sparse table of swaps (columns tomato, basil, sunflower); 7.2 the tomato column glows green, "who swapped it: Ada, Cy, Dot"; 9.4 a grey tag "many categorical features" and, on the CSR card, red "slow for one column". Hold to 12.

points.head:
Order = how many indices
find one value

Sparse: mostly zeros,
so store only the non-zeros

CSR for rows,
CSC for columns

recap.spec: Lecture 14 (ds-14) · scene 11-recap: three rows, each a small pictogram that plays once and holds, and one bold line (bare). Story (local seconds): 0.1 title and Pebble; rows slide in at 0.8 / 1.9 / 3.0, each pictogram runs on its row's own clock (q = t − row time) and is finished by q 2.4; 4.2 the call to action "Next: Workshop 14.W". Rows are done at about 3.2, 4.3 and 5.4; after that only Pebble's bob moves. Row 1 (purple): a cube, a row, a grid and a pile of grids pop in left to right (q 0.6 / 1.0 / 1.4 / 1.8): order 0 to 3. Row 2 (blue): a faint 4 x 4 grid with three blue cells (q 0.6); q 1.1-1.5 a grey arrow draws; q 1.5-2.1 three blue chips pop into a short list (only the non-zeros are kept). Row 3 (green): three short arrays (blue V, orange COL_INDEX, purple ROW_INDEX) and a small grid; q 1.0 a green frame on one row of the grid (CSR), q 1.8 a green frame on one column (CSC); both stay.
